text: The sexton stood in the porch of the Milford meeting house, pulling busily at the bell rope, while the old people of the village came stooping along the street. <break time="0.8s" /> But what has good Parson Hooper got upon his face, cried the sexton in astonishment, as the minister came slowly along the street toward the meeting house. <break time="0.8s" /> Mister Hooper, a gentlemanly man of about thirty who was still a bachelor, was dressed neatly, but there was one thing remarkable in his appearance. <break time="0.8s" /> Swathed about his forehead and hanging down over his face was a black veil, which entirely concealed his features except the mouth and chin. <break time="0.8s" /> Our parson has gone mad, cried Goodman Gray, and a strange murmur spread through the meeting house as the veiled minister walked slowly up the aisle. <break time="0.8s" /> Many people turned around in their seats to stare, and several little boys climbed upon the benches and came down again with a terrible racket. <break time="0.8s" /> That day he preached about secret sin, about the sad mysteries which we hide from our nearest and dearest, and even from our own consciousness. <break time="0.8s" /> Each member of the congregation, even the most innocent girl, felt as if the preacher had crept upon them behind his awful veil and discovered their hidden sins.
